The primary works but its scores are low. Its validation mean recall@10 is 0.0335, about 6x chance (≈0.0054). It beats CCA (0.0179) in 4/4 folds, by +0.016 ± 0.008. For image-to-expression prediction it only ties ridge: Pearson on the top 50 genes is 0.150 vs 0.152, and the primary is better in just 2/4 folds. The automatic flag calls hard_infonce's gain on recall@10 'within noise', but it beat the primary in every fold: +0.0043, +0.0041, +0.0084, +0.0101 (mean +0.0067, SD ≈0.003). patch_context_2x was also better in 4/4 folds, by less (+0.0025). The soft-target loss was chosen because 23% of spots have near-twins, but the evidence goes against that choice. On the same folds, hard InfoNCE gave higher recall@10 for every held-out patient group, by about 20% relative (0.040 vs 0.0335). A paired comparison over four folds gives t ≈ 4.5, which is small evidence but consistent. Switching needs no extra compute: the per-fold results already exist and already beat the primary. One caveat: all scores are best-epoch scores picked on validation, so they are slightly optimistic, but that bias is the same for both configurations. Training curves show early peaks (best epochs 3–10) in every configuration, and hard InfoNCE overfits faster (train loss falls to about 1.6 while validation scores drift down). Early stopping already copes with this.
